title: Pixel Art
summary: Visible square pixels. Small palettes. Stepped edges and bitmap type.
lede: Pictures and interfaces built from visible square pixels in a small palette, after the graphics of 8-bit and 16-bit computers, arcade machines, and game consoles. This record covers that core look in interfaces and graphics.

era.note: The core look comes from arcade games such as Space Invaders (1978) and the 8-bit and 16-bit consoles and home computers of the 1980s and 1990s. The term was first published in 1982. Independent games revived it from the 2010s, and it is still in use.

attestation.label: Wikipedia: Pixel art. Defines the form, ties it to 8-bit and 16-bit era graphics, and dates the first published use of the term to Goldberg and Flegal, Xerox PARC, 1982.
Wikidata Q811179: pixel art, an instance of art genre and a subclass of digital art.
Wikipedia: Susan Kare. Calls her a pioneer of pixel art and of the graphical computer interface, for the first Apple Macintosh (1983–1986).
NES.css on GitHub: a "NES-style CSS Framework" for web interfaces, MIT license, created 2018.

lineage.label: Video game art
lineage.note: Wikipedia says pixel art as it is known today largely originates from the golden age of arcade video games and 8-bit consoles such as the Nintendo Entertainment System (1983).

lineage.label: Mosaic
lineage.note: Wikipedia names mosaic, cross-stitch, and beadwork as non-digital counterparts that build pictures from small colored units.

lineage.label: Cross-stitch
lineage.note: Wikipedia names counted-thread embroidery, including cross-stitch, as a possible predecessor.

lineage.label: Demoscene
lineage.note: Wikipedia describes demoscene graphicians publishing pixel art in demos from the late 1980s and holding pixel graphics competitions in the 1990s.
Wikipedia says synthwave artists used pixel art for music videos in the 2010s, for example for Perturbator and Gunship.

grammar.text: Every size, gap, outline, and step is a whole multiple of one enlarged pixel, often 4 px on screen.
Frames are drawn pixel by pixel: hard outlines with notched corners and one-step bevels. No anti-aliasing, blur, or gloss.
Monospaced or bitmap pixel faces in one weight, often in capitals, for headings, labels, and counters.
About 8 to 16 saturated, hardware-like colors with black and a light ground. Shading is in flat palette steps or checkerboard dithering, not gradients.
Small characters, items, and icons drawn at low resolution and enlarged by whole numbers, so each pixel stays square. Tiled ground and sky strips.
Title screens, menu windows, dialogue boxes, score counters, and status bars organize the page.
Animation steps between a few frames, such as a blinking cursor or a two-frame sprite, with no easing.

synthesis: Game assets and bitmap fonts carry the core. The [DawnLike tileset](ref:dawnlike-tileset-2014) fits every wall, floor, and monster to a 16-pixel cell in one 16-color palette, with flat shading in two or three steps. The [Kenney 1-Bit Pack](ref:kenney-1-bit-pack-2019) reduces the style to one color per object on a 16-pixel grid, with a bitmap alphabet and the game furniture that the rubric names: hearts, coins, keys, and frames. The [Liberated Pixel Cup base assets](ref:liberated-pixel-cup-base-assets-2012) show the 16-bit end: 32-pixel sprites, outlines in a dark shade of the skin color, and a nine-frame walk cycle with no tweening. [Press Start 2P](ref:press-start-2p-typeface) is a heading face on an 8 × 8 arcade cell, and [Silkscreen](ref:silkscreen-typeface) is a label face with 5-pixel capitals.

The historical anchors are documented, not observed, because their images are in copyright. [Space Invaders](ref:space-invaders-1978) (1978) is the source of the two-frame motion rule and of flat color bands from cellophane strips. [Susan Kare’s Macintosh icons](ref:kare-macintosh-icons-1984) show one-bit pictograms and bitmap type at the scale of an operating system. The [Goldberg and Flegal letter](ref:goldberg-flegal-pixel-art-letter-1982) is the first published use of the term; its text was not read. Recent games show the style at full screen: [Pixel Dungeon](ref:pixel-dungeon-2012) and [Mindustry](ref:mindustry-2019) draw buttons, counters, and text on the same pixel scale as the map, and [Hotline Miami](ref:hotline-miami-2012) and [VA-11 Hall-A](ref:va-11-hall-a-video-game-2016) use neon palettes. Three references are partial fits at the edges: [PixelPlaza’s pirate lair](ref:pixelplaza-pirate-lair-2008) is the isometric branch with about 250 colors, [Design Quarterly 133](ref:greiman-design-quarterly-133-1986) puts a bitmap self-portrait in a New Wave layout, and [Agora Road](ref:agora-road-website) puts pixel fonts and a dithered figure inside a vaporwave collage.

The references disagree with the grammar in two places. First, color: the grammar asks for saturated colors with a light ground, but the stored game images have dark, muted grounds. DawnLike measures lightness 0.24 and chroma 0.11 on #140c1c, Kenney 0.36 and 0.13 on #472d3c, and Pixel Dungeon 0.21 and 0.05 on black. Saturated full-screen palettes appear only in Hotline Miami and VA-11 Hall-A, which are not stored. The DawnLike record concludes that a small fixed palette, not saturation, is the core trait. Second, smoothness: the counter-rubric rejects smooth gradients, blur, and glows, but Pixel Dungeon lays a smooth vignette and a lamp glow over its map, Mindustry draws translucent range circles, and Hotline Miami, a clear fit, fills the area outside the building with a pink-to-magenta gradient. Three of the four recent games are thus hybrids with smooth effects over pixel sprites, a branch that the record scopes out.

The record is scoped to the 8-bit and 16-bit core. Isometric pixel art (Wikipedia names Habbo Hotel and eBoy), pixel dolls, photorealistic demoscene work with anti-aliasing, and high-definition hybrids that mix pixel sprites with smooth effects are related branches.

The fingerprint reads CSS, and the collection has no clear pixel-art website. The one capture, Agora Road, is a partial fit and passes two of seven rules: `surface.shadow.hardShare` (1) and `surface.radius.median` (0). It fails `type.monoShare` (0.18 against a minimum of 0.6; the value equals the share of the PerfectDOSVGA437 font, so the Chicago bitmap face, 0.17, does not count as monospaced), `surface.shadow.share` (0.29 against 0.4), `surface.shadow.medianOffset` (1.4 px against 2 to 6, the 1 px Windows bevel), `color.patternShare` (0.06 against 0.1), and `color.gradientShare` (0.07 against a maximum of 0.02). The image measurements cannot count a palette exactly: the Kenney sheet has exactly 8 colors and measures 14 distinct, and the two-color Press Start 2P specimen measures 4, probably because the tool counts blended tones. The PixelPlaza measurement gives black as its largest color (0.239), but the record observes a white ground, so transparent pixels are probably read as black. The fingerprint stays specimen-based until pixel-art websites are captured.

diagnostic: Square pixels are visible and placed by hand: curves and diagonals step like staircases.
Colors come from a small fixed palette. Shading is in flat steps or checkerboard dithering.
Frames and buttons have hard pixel outlines with notched corners or one-pixel bevels.
Headings and labels use a bitmap or monospaced pixel face, often in capitals.
Sprites, tiles, and game furniture appear: dialogue boxes, menu cursors, hearts, coins, score counters.
counter: Smooth anti-aliased curves, blur, glows, or smooth gradients on the main surfaces.
Pixels enlarged by uneven factors, so they look blurred or have different sizes.
A photograph run through a pixelate filter, with no deliberate placement of pixels.

confusions.difference: Minimalist Machine is quiet and neutral: thin 1 px rules, sans-serif headings, and at most one signal color. Pixel art uses chunky stepped frames, bitmap type throughout, several saturated palette colors, and sprites.

Y2K is chrome, silver, translucent candy plastic, glows, and rounded capsules with smooth gradients. Pixel art has no gradients or glows: shading is flat palette steps and dithering, and corners are square or stepped.

Vaporwave quotes high-resolution 1990s desktop windows with 1 px bevels, pastel pink and purple, Greek statues, and collage. It can put pixel images inside the collage. Pixel art draws the whole surface on one coarse pixel grid, with bitmap type and saturated game palettes.
Neo-brutalism uses smooth thick black outlines, offset block shadows, and large sans-serif type. Pixel art outlines step at the corners, the type is bitmap, and the page adds sprites and dithering.
Glitch art shows corrupted or broken digital images: smeared rows, shifted channels, noise. Pixel art places clean pixels on purpose on a stable grid.
ASCII art builds pictures from text characters. Pixel art builds them from colored square pixels.
Voxel art builds three-dimensional models from cubes, usually rendered with smooth lighting. Pixel art is flat and two-dimensional.

do: Choose one pixel unit, for example 4 px, and make every size, outline, and gap a whole multiple of it.
Limit the palette to about 8 to 16 colors. Shade with palette steps or checkerboard dithering.
Draw frames with hard, unblurred outlines and notched corners. Give buttons a one-unit bevel that moves when pressed.
Enlarge pixel images by whole numbers and set image-rendering: pixelated.
Use a bitmap or monospaced face for headings and labels. Keep body text at a readable size and line length.
Animate in steps, and stop the animation when the user asks for reduced motion.
dont: Do not blur, smooth, or anti-alias edges, shadows, or enlarged sprites.
Do not use smooth gradients, glows, or rounded corners.
Do not set long body text in a small pixel font.
Do not mix pixel sizes in one view. A sprite drawn with 2 px pixels next to one drawn with 8 px pixels breaks the grid.
Do not run a photograph through a pixelate filter and call it pixel art.
uses: Independent game sites, press kits, and game jams
Hobby software, developer side projects, and command-line tool sites with a playful tone
Chiptune music, retro computing, and demoscene pages
Achievement badges, progress bars, and other game-like interface details
avoid: Long-form reading such as documentation or news. Bitmap type tires readers over long text.
Healthcare, finance, and legal services. The style reads as a game, not as calm and serious.
Luxury and premium brands. The coarse grid reads as cheap or nostalgic.
Dashboards with fine charts and dense data. The coarse pixel unit cannot show fine detail.

fingerprint.note: Bitmap or monospaced type carries most text, not only labels. The specimen measures 1; no other specimen measures more than 0.3. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references. Sites that load a pixel webfont without a monospace fallback in the stack measure 0 here.

Most windows, buttons, and fields carry a stepped pixel frame. The specimen draws the frames with hard shadows and measures 0.66. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references.
Stepped outlines and bevels are drawn with unblurred shadows, not glows. The specimen measures 1. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references.

Outlines step by one enlarged pixel, 2 to 6 px on screen. Not the 8 px or larger blocks of offset-shadow styles. The specimen measures 4. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references.

A tiled or dithered strip covers part of the page. The specimen measures 0.25. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references. Sites that draw tiles as images measure 0 here.
